tasks.title: Project Setup and Configuration (Java 21 + Spring Boot 3.5.4)
tasks.description: Initialize the MOAPIN backend project with Gradle (Groovy DSL), configure core dependencies/services, environments, and provide a health endpoint.
tasks.details:
Implementation steps:

- Add dependencies: spring-boot-starter-web, spring-boot-starter-validation, spring-boot-starter-security, spring-boot-starter-data-jpa, postgresql, flyway-core, bucket4j-core (and filter integration), io.jsonwebtoken:jjwt-api/impl/jackson (0.12+), de.mkammerer:argon2-jvm, io.minio:minio (latest 8.x), com.meilisearch.sdk:meilisearch-java, software.amazon.awssdk:sesv2, lombok (optional), springdoc-openapi-ui (optional for docs), testcontainers (postgresql, junit, mockmvc), awaitility.
- Configure application.yml (and application-local.yml) with placeholders for: DB URL, username/password; MinIO endpoint, access/secret, region, bucket; MeiliSearch host and master key; AWS SES region/credentials; JWT secret, expiration; feature flags: USE_EXTERNAL_AI=false, EXTERNAL_AI_PROVIDER=openai.
- Flyway baseline migration V1__init.sql for base schemas placeholder (or empty; detailed schemas added in later tasks).
- Provide simple HealthController: GET /health -> 200 OK {status: "ok"}.
- Configure logging patterns and JSON logging if desired; include UTC as default server TZ but ensure we handle Asia/Seoul where needed.
- Docker Compose (dev) to run Postgres, MinIO, MeiliSearch, LocalStack (for SES) services.
Pseudo-code: build.gradle
plugins { id 'java'; id 'org.springframework.boot' version '3.5.4'; id 'io.spring.dependency-management' version '1.1.6' }
java { toolchain { languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(21) } }
dependencies { implementation 'org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-web' ... }

application.yml (snippets)
app:
  jwt:
    secret: ${JWT_SECRET}
    accessTokenTtlMinutes: 60
  ai:
    useExternal: ${USE_EXTERNAL_AI:false}
    provider: ${EXTERNAL_AI_PROVIDER:openai}
spring:
  datasource: ...
  jpa:
    hibernate.ddl-auto: validate
    properties.hibernate.default_schema: public
server:
  servlet.context-path: /
tasks.testStrategy:
- Build verification: gradle build succeeds, Spring Boot app starts.
- Health endpoint integration test with MockMvc: GET /health returns 200 and JSON body.
- Verify external service connectivity locally via Docker Compose (Postgres, MinIO, MeiliSearch, LocalStack SES) smoke tests.

tasks.title: User Authentication (Signup/Login/JWT)
tasks.description: Implement secure user registration and login. Use Argon2id for password hashing, issue stateless JWTs, and secure endpoints with Spring Security.
tasks.details:
Implementation steps:
- Entity: users(id UUID PK, username unique, email unique, password_hash, created_at, updated_at, last_login_at). Add Flyway migration V2__users.sql.
- Repositories: UserRepository (Spring Data JPA).
- DTOs (Java records): SignupRequest(username, email, password), LoginRequest(usernameOrEmail, password), AuthResponse(token, userId, username, email).
- Password hashing: Argon2id using de.mkammerer.argon2 Argon2Factory.create(Argon2Factory.Argon2Types.ARGON2id). Store password_hash.
- JWT: HS256 tokens via jjwt. Use strong 256-bit secret from env. Claims: sub=userId, username, exp. Access token TTL from config.
- Security: Stateless SecurityFilterChain; permitAll for /api/auth/** and /share/**, authenticate others; add JWT authentication filter parsing Authorization: Bearer.
- Rate limiting: Bucket4j-based filter for /api/auth/login (e.g., 5 attempts/min per IP and per username). Return 429 on exceed.
- Validation: Unique username/email checks; password strength (length >= 10, mix of chars); email format.
- Endpoints:
  - POST /api/auth/signup: validate, hash, save, 201 created.
  - POST /api/auth/login: authenticate credentials; on success, issue JWT and update last_login_at.
  - POST /api/auth/logout: no-op (client disposes token); return 200.
- Authorization utilities: @AuthenticationPrincipal to inject userId into controllers.
Pseudo-code (login):
User u = userRepo.findByUsernameOrEmail(req.usernameOrEmail())
if u == null || !argon2.verify(u.password_hash, req.password()) throw 401
String jwt = Jwts.builder().subject(u.id.toString()).claim("username", u.username).expiration(now+ttl).signWith(key, HS256).compact()
return AuthResponse(jwt, u.id, u.username, u.email)
tasks.testStrategy:
- Unit: Password hashing and verification; JWT generation/validation; rate limiter logic.
- Integration: MockMvc tests for signup/login happy and failure paths (duplicate username/email, weak password, invalid creds -> 401).
- Security: Accessing protected endpoint without/with token returns 401/200; token expiry test.
- Flyway migrations apply cleanly on Testcontainers Postgres.

tasks.title: Password Reset Flow via AWS SES
tasks.description: Implement secure password reset using time-limited, one-time tokens and Amazon SES to deliver reset links.
tasks.details:
Implementation steps:
- Entity: password_reset_tokens(id UUID PK, user_id FK, token varchar(64) unique, expires_at timestamptz, used_at timestamptz null, created_at).
  Flyway V3__password_reset.sql.
- Service: PasswordResetService to create token and validate/consume it.
- Token generation: SecureRandom 32 bytes -> Base64 URL-safe string; expiry 1 hour.
- SES client: SesV2Client configured with region and credentials from env. Verified sender address from env (EMAIL_FROM).
- Email: Templated link to frontend, e.g. ${FRONTEND_URL}/reset-password?token=... or backend confirm path. Keep body simple HTML/text.
- Endpoints:
  - POST /api/auth/password-reset-request {email}: Always 200. If user exists, create token and send email.
  - POST /api/auth/password-reset-confirm {token, newPassword}: Validate token exists, not used, not expired; update user password (Argon2), set used_at; 200 on success.
- Security & UX: Do not leak whether email exists; enforce strong password; invalidate token after use.
Pseudo-code (request):
optUser = userRepo.findByEmail(email)
if (optUser.isPresent()) { token = genToken(); saveToken(user, token, now+1h); ses.sendEmail(EmailContent with link) }
return 200
tasks.testStrategy:
- Unit: Token generation length/entropy; expiry checks.
- Integration: Request then confirm flow on Testcontainers with mock SES (LocalStack) or SES client stub; verify password changed and token marked used.
- Negative tests: expired token -> 400, reused token -> 400; non-existent token -> 400.
- Security: Ensure request endpoint returns 200 even for unknown email; ensure password is Argon2-hashed.

tasks.details:

- Relationship: user -> categories (FK with ON DELETE CASCADE as appropriate).
- Endpoints:
  - GET /api/categories?sort={createdDate|modifiedDate|views|custom}
    - For views sorting: LEFT JOIN contents, SUM(view_count) GROUP BY category id; if heavy, fall back to createdDate/modifiedDate first.
  - POST /api/categories {name}
  - PUT /api/categories/{id} {name}
  - DELETE /api/categories/{id}: Cascade delete contents (and their related data) in service layer and DB FKs.
  - PUT /api/categories/reorder { ids: [catId...] }: Set order_index by position.
- Return contentCount per category in list via COUNT(contents.id).
- Authorization: Always filter by authenticated user_id.
- Cascade strategy: DB FKs with ON DELETE CASCADE for contents; service ensures delete of MinIO objects handled when content deletion executes (content service method invoked by cascade hook or pre-delete fetch).
Pseudo-code (reorder):
for (int i=0; i<ids.size(); i++) { catRepo.updateOrderIndexIfOwned(ids.get(i), i, userId) }

tasks.description: Implement content lifecycle for photos/links/notes, presigned file handling with MinIO, tagging, view counting, and pin/bookmarks.
tasks.details:
Implementation steps:
- Entities and migrations (Flyway V5__content_tags.sql):
  - contents(id UUID PK, user_id FK, category_id FK, type enum('photo','link','note'), title text null, body text null, url text null, file_path text null, view_count bigint default 0, is_pinned boolean default false, is_reviewed boolean default false, summary text null, created_at, updated_at).
  - tags(id UUID PK, user_id FK, name varchar(64), unique(user_id,name)).
  - content_tags(content_id FK, tag_id FK, PK(content_id, tag_id)).
- MinIO: Configure client. Ensure bucket exists on startup (create if missing). Presigned URLs:
  - POST /api/content/presigned-url {filename, contentType} -> generate unique key like userId/yyyy/MM/dd/uuid_filename, return presigned PUT URL (expiry 10-15 min) and object key.
  - GET /api/content/download-url/{id} -> verify ownership and type=photo, return presigned GET URL (short expiry, e.g., 5 min).
- Endpoints:
  - POST /api/content {categoryId, type, title?, body?/url?/fileKey?, tags?[]} -> validate type-specific fields; if photo, require fileKey from upload step; persist content and tag associations (create tags if new for user).
  - GET /api/content?category={id}&sort={createdAt|views|updatedAt}&tag={t?}&pinnedFirst=true -> list content; pinned items first if requested or always for category listing per PRD.
  - GET /api/content/{id} -> return full details; increment view_count atomically.
  - PUT /api/content/{id} -> edit fields, move category (validate ownership), manage tags (replace set), toggle is_pinned and is_reviewed if included.
  - DELETE /api/content/{id} -> delete DB record and if photo, delete object from MinIO.
  - POST /api/content/{id}/pin {pinned:true|false} -> convenience endpoint to toggle pin.
  - GET /api/content/bookmarks -> list all is_pinned=true items for user across categories.
- Validation: max upload size via gateway (client) + server-side check by metadata; allowed photo content types (image/jpeg, png, webp); note body length cap (e.g., 50k chars); max 20 tags, each <= 32 chars.
- View counting: use repository method with JPQL/SQL atomic increment: UPDATE contents SET view_count=view_count+1 WHERE id=:id AND user_id=:userId.
- Concurrency/consistency: wrap operations in @Transactional; ensure MinIO operations are attempted after DB success; on delete failure to remove object, log and enqueue retry (optional) but do not block.
Pseudo-code (presigned upload):
String key = String.format("%s/%s/%s_%s", userId, LocalDate.now(), UUID.randomUUID(), sanitize(filename))
String url = minio.getPresignedObjectUrl(PutObjectArgs.builder().bucket(bucket).object(key).contentType(ct).expiry(15, MINUTES).build())
return { key, url }

tasks.title: Shareable Links: Generation, Management, and Public Access
tasks.description: Implement secure share links with expiration, download limits, revoke, and public access to a single content item.
tasks.details:
Implementation steps:
- Entity: share_links(id UUID PK, content_id FK, token varchar(64) unique, expires_at timestamptz null, max_downloads int null, download_count int default 0, is_revoked boolean default false, created_at, created_by user_id). Flyway V6__share_links.sql.
- Service: ShareLinkService for CRUD and validations.
- Endpoints (auth):
  - POST /api/share {contentId, expireDays?, maxDownloads?}: create link; token via SecureRandom (32 bytes, Base64 URL-safe). If expireDays, set expires_at = now + days; return token and URL (BASE_URL/share/{token}).
  - GET /api/share: list active links for user.
  - DELETE /api/share/{id}: revoke by setting is_revoked=true or delete row.
- Public endpoint (no auth): GET /share/{token}
  - Validate token exists, not revoked, not expired, and download_count < max if set.
  - If content.type=photo: generate presigned GET from MinIO and 302 redirect to that URL.
  - If content.type=note or link: render a simple HTML page with content text or link anchor (Content-Security-Policy minimal). Alternatively return JSON if Accept: application/json.
  - Increment share_links.download_count and contents.view_count atomically.
  - If invalid or expired: return 410 Gone (or 404) with simple HTML message.
- Logging: record access events at info for observability.
Pseudo-code (public access):
sl = repo.findByToken(token)
if invalid -> 410
content = contentRepo.find(sl.content_id)
if content.type=='photo' -> redirect( presignedGetUrl(content.file_path) )
else -> return HTML page built from template
repo.incrementDownloadCount(sl.id); contentRepo.incrementViewCount(content.id)

tasks.title: Reminders & Scheduled Email Notifications (KST)
tasks.description: Allow users to schedule reminders for content and send SES emails at the configured time. Provide management endpoints and mark content as reviewed.
tasks.details:
Implementation steps:
- Entity: reminders(id UUID PK, user_id FK, content_id FK, remind_at timestamptz, created_at, sent_at timestamptz null). Unique constraint (user_id, content_id, sent_at is null) if we allow only one active per content. Flyway V8__reminders.sql.
- Endpoints:
  - POST /api/reminders {contentId, remindAt}: validate ownership; remindAt must be in future; create.
  - GET /api/reminders: list active (sent_at is null and remind_at > now) or include both with filters.
  - DELETE /api/reminders/{id}: cancel (delete or mark canceled if column added).
  - POST /api/content/{id}/mark-reviewed: set contents.is_reviewed=true.
- Scheduler: @Scheduled(cron="0 * * * * *", zone="Asia/Seoul") every minute.
  - Query reminders where sent_at is null and remind_at <= now(KST). For each: send SES email (subject "MOAPIN Reminder: {title}", body includes link to app deep link with contentId). Set sent_at=now.
- Time handling: Store timestamps in UTC; interpret/display using Asia/Seoul; Scheduler uses zone="Asia/Seoul".
- Deletions: On content delete, cascade delete reminders (FK ON DELETE CASCADE) or remove in service.
Pseudo-code (scheduler):
List<Reminder> due = repo.findDue(nowKST)
for (r : due) { sendEmail(r.user.email, buildBody(r.content)); r.sent_at = Instant.now(); repo.save(r) }

- Unit: Validation for future times; KST conversion using Clock and ZoneId.
- Integration: Create reminder with near-future time; run scheduler (advance clock or wait) and assert email sent via LocalStack SES; sent_at set.
- Mark-reviewed endpoint sets flag; list reminders returns expected; delete cancels.
- Ensure no duplicate sends (idempotency via sent_at).

tasks.description: Aggregate usage metrics nightly (KST), store daily stats, and expose APIs for daily/weekly/monthly reports.
tasks.details:
Implementation steps:
- Entity: user_stats_daily(id bigserial PK, user_id FK, date date (KST), new_content_count int, total_content_count int, total_views_cumulative bigint, created_at). Flyway V9__stats_daily.sql. Add unique(user_id, date).
- Nightly job: @Scheduled(cron="0 0 2 * * *", zone="Asia/Seoul"). For each user:
  - Compute period [yesterday 00:00..23:59 KST].
  - new_content_count = COUNT(contents WHERE created_at in window).
  - total_content_count = COUNT(contents WHERE created_at <= window.end).
  - total_views_cumulative = SUM(contents.view_count) at job time.
  - UPSERT into user_stats_daily.
- APIs:
  - GET /api/stats/daily?days=30 -> return array [ {date, newContent, totalContent, totalViewsCumulative} ].
  - GET /api/stats/weekly?weeks=12 and /api/stats/monthly?months=12 -> compute by aggregating user_stats_daily on the fly (sum groups of 7 days; by calendar month), or precompute if needed later.
  - GET /api/stats/summary -> quick totals (from live DB): total contents by type, total views, counts by category.
- Indexing: DB indexes on contents.created_at, contents.user_id, and stats unique index.
Pseudo-code (daily job):
LocalDate y = LocalDate.now(kst).minusDays(1)
ZonedDateTime start = y.atStartOfDay(kst); ZonedDateTime end = y.atTime(LocalTime.MAX).withZoneSameInstant(kst)
int newCnt = contentRepo.countCreatedBetween(userId, start.toInstant(), end.toInstant())
int totalCnt = contentRepo.countCreatedBeforeEq(userId, end.toInstant())
long totalViews = contentRepo.sumViewCount(userId)
statsRepo.upsert(userId, y, newCnt, totalCnt, totalViews)

tasks.title: AI Summarization & Auto-Tagging (Internal + Optional External Fallback)
tasks.description: Provide asynchronous AI analysis to summarize notes/links and suggest tags, with a local lightweight algorithm and optional external provider (OpenAI) via env flag.
tasks.details:
Implementation steps:
- Configuration: app.ai.useExternal (bool), app.ai.provider=openai, OPENAI_API_KEY env. Implement provider interface AiClient { SummaryAndTags analyze(String text) } with two implementations: LocalAiClient and OpenAiClient.
- Local AI:
  - Summarization: naive extractive summary: choose first sentence up to N chars (e.g., 200), or simple TextRank implementation if feasible.
  - Tagging: tokenize (split on non-alphanumerics), lowercase, remove stopwords (EN/KR lists), count frequencies, return top N unique keywords (3-7). Deduplicate with existing tags.
- External AI (optional): call OpenAI Chat Completions with a concise prompt to produce JSON {summary: "...", tags: ["..."]}. Use small model (e.g., gpt-4o-mini) for cost. Strict JSON mode and robust parsing; timeouts and retries.
- Workflow:
  - On content creation (type note or link with body/title): submit async task (@Async or ApplicationEvent) to run AI.
  - Choose provider: if useExternal==true then external else local (or fall back to local on error).
  - Persist results: update contents.summary and merge suggested tags into content_tags (create Tag rows if needed). Emit Outbox UPDATE event for search reindex.
- Endpoints (optional but helpful):
  - POST /api/content/{id}/ai-analyze: manual trigger; returns current summary/tags after processing.
  - GET /api/content/{id}/summary and /suggested-tags (or include in GET content).
- Error handling: catch and log exceptions; do not block content creation. Rate-limit external API calls if necessary.
Pseudo-code (async listener):
@EventListener
public void onContentCreated(ContentCreatedEvent e) {
  if (!isTextual(e.content)) return;
  SummaryAndTags res = aiClient.analyze(e.content.text())
  content.setSummary(res.summary()); tagService.mergeSuggested(e.content.id, res.tags());
  contentRepo.save(content); outbox.add(UPDATE)
}

subtasks.title: Concurrency control and SKIP LOCKED processing
subtasks.description: Ensure multi-instance safe processing using SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and idempotent status transitions.
subtasks.details:
- Repository native queries for PostgreSQL: 
  1) fetchDueForUpdate(now, limit): SELECT id FROM reminder WHERE status='PENDING' AND remind_at <= :now ORDER BY remind_at ASC, id ASC FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT :limit.
  2) markProcessing(id, now) with WHERE status='PENDING'.
  3) markSent(id) with WHERE status='PROCESSING'.
  4) markPendingFromProcessing(id) on failure.
- Dispatcher flow: attempt markProcessing before publish; only when rowsAffected=1 proceed.
- Add transactional boundaries: each reminder processed in REQUIRES_NEW with timeout to avoid long locks.
- Document requirement for PostgreSQL; provide fallback JPQL without SKIP LOCKED guarded behind profile/local.
